What we do, and how we do it.

A five-phase delivery approach with named deliverables, client inputs, review points, and an operating handover. Start with a pilot, then scale what works.

  1. 1

    Discover

    1–2 weeks

    We map how enquiries, orders, production data, quality records and dispatch actually flow today, sit with the order desk, estimators and plant teams, and pick the workflows where automation helps most. We baseline the KPIs from existing ERP and CRM data and identify GST, GxP and data protection boundaries early.

    Deliverables

    • Current-state process maps for the selected workflows
    • Data source inventory covering ERP or Tally, MES, CRM and marketplaces
    • Prioritized automation backlog with effort and risk
    • KPI baseline and measurement plan

    What we need from you

    • Read access or sample exports from the ERP or Tally, CRM and marketplace accounts
    • Time with sales coordinators, estimators, the order desk, plant and QA leads
    • Existing SOPs, approval matrices and credit policies
  2. 2

    Design

    1–2 weeks

    We design each workflow with its triggers, data fields, decision rules, approval points and failure paths, plus the WhatsApp templates and review screens people will use. For regulated sites we agree with QA where each automation sits relative to validated systems and what change control it needs.

    Deliverables

    • Workflow designs with human checkpoints and exception paths
    • Integration plan for ERP, GSP, marketplace and messaging APIs
    • WhatsApp template drafts and review-screen or portal prototypes
    • Access, consent and retention design

    What we need from you

    • Pricing, credit and quality decision rules approved by their owners
    • Message and notice wording reviewed by the client's legal or compliance owner
    • QA input on the change control route for GxP-adjacent workflows
  3. 3

    Build

    2–6 weeks

    We build integrations, workflows, review screens and dashboards in a test environment, using sample or anonymized data where possible, with logging, alerts and role-based access from the start. Each workflow is demonstrated to its owners as it takes shape.

    Deliverables

    • Working workflows in a test environment
    • ERP, CRM, marketplace and WhatsApp integrations
    • Review and approval screens for estimators, the order desk and QA
    • Dashboards built on the agreed KPI definitions
    • Run logs, alerts and error handling

    What we need from you

    • API credentials or service accounts with least-privilege access
    • WhatsApp Business account verification and template submissions
    • Test data and named testers from each team
  4. 4

    Validate & launch

    1–2 weeks

    Owners test each workflow against real scenarios, including credit holds, partial dispatches, e-way bill extensions and low-confidence AI extractions. We launch to a pilot group first, run alongside the existing process for a short period, and train the people who approve work and handle exceptions.

    Deliverables

    • User acceptance test results signed off by owners
    • Parallel-run comparison against the current process
    • Training for approvers and exception handlers
    • Go-live checklist and rollback plan

    What we need from you

    • Named owners to sign off each workflow
    • A pilot group of reps, dealers, estimators or plant users
    • Completion of the site's change control steps for GxP-adjacent workflows
  5. 5

    Operate & improve

    Ongoing, with monthly reviews

    We monitor runs, failures and AI accuracy, review KPIs with the owners each month, tune rules and prompts, and add the next workflows from the backlog. Every change follows the same design, test and approval route as the original build.

    Deliverables

    • Monthly KPI and exception review
    • Sampled AI accuracy checks with prompt and rule updates
    • Incident log with fixes and preventive actions
    • Updated backlog and roadmap

    What we need from you

    • Monthly review time with the business owner
    • Feedback from users and exception handlers
    • Advance notice of changes to ERP fields, price lists, schemes or SOPs

First pilot: Enquiry-to-quote pilot for one product family

A four to six week pilot that connects IndiaMART, website forms and the RFQ inbox for one product family, routes qualified enquiries to their owners and gives the estimator a costing draft to approve. Pharma plants can instead pilot a read-only batch release board for one product line, timed around change control. We compare first-response and quote turnaround with the baseline and decide together whether to extend.

  • Enquiry capture from the IndiaMART Lead Manager API, website forms and one RFQ mailbox
  • Extraction, deduplication and routing rules for one product family and region
  • Costing draft and estimator review screen for repeat items that already have cost data
  • Response-time and quote-turnaround dashboard compared with the baseline
  • Training for sales coordinators and estimators, followed by a go or no-go review

Ways to work together

Choose the engagement that fits your stage.

  • Pilot sprint

    One automation, one segment and one accountable owner. We build, validate and measure it against agreed acceptance criteria before anything wider is committed.

    Best for: Proving value and fit with low risk

  • Phased rollout

    A prioritized roadmap across the journey, released in reviewed increments, with training and documentation after each release.

    Best for: Teams ready to connect several workflows

  • Operate & improve

    Monthly reviews of measures and exceptions, template and rule updates, and new automations as priorities change, during business hours.

    Best for: Keeping automations accurate as the business changes

Safe by design, owned by your team

  • The ERP stays the system of record. Automations write only drafts or agreed status fields; invoices, e-invoices, e-way bills and journal entries are created only by authorized users in the ERP or GST systems.
  • A written approval matrix names who decides prices, discounts, credit holds, quality dispositions, maintenance deferrals and batch release, and every approval is logged against that person.
  • On GxP sites, automations sit outside validated systems, read status only and are introduced through the site's change control; no GxP record or signature is created, altered or deleted.
  • Personal data is minimized: consent records for WhatsApp contacts, role-based access, agreed retention periods per data type, and breach response steps designed around the DPDP Act and Rules.
  • AI output is labeled as a draft with links to its sources, low-confidence cases go to people, and samples are checked for accuracy every month.
  • Every workflow has run logs, failure alerts, an owner for exceptions and a rollback plan, and credentials are stored in a secrets vault with least-privilege access.

The obligations that shape the design

Implementation notes, not legal advice. Your legal or compliance owner confirms how each obligation applies to your organization.

  • GST e-invoicing and e-way bills

    Most businesses whose aggregate turnover in any year since 2017-18 exceeded ₹5 crore must report B2B and export invoices to the Invoice Registration Portal; since April 1, 2025, those with AATO of ₹10 crore or more cannot report an invoice more than 30 days after its date. E-way bills cannot be generated on documents older than 180 days. Workflows read IRN and e-way bill status and alert people; they never generate, cancel or extend them.

    einvoice1.gst.gov.in · Source

  • Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and DPDP Rules, 2025

    Buyer contacts, dealer staff, field reps and service customers are data principals. The DPDP Rules were notified in November 2025 with phased commencement, and duties on notice, consent, security safeguards, breach intimation and data principal rights apply from May 2027 under the notified schedule. We design clear notices, purpose-limited fields, role-based access, retention limits and breach response steps now. GDPR may also apply to contacts in the EU.

    pib.gov.in · Source

  • Revised Schedule M and GxP electronic records

    Licensed drug manufacturers must meet revised Schedule M (G.S.R. 922(E), December 2023), which adds a pharmaceutical quality system, quality risk management and controls on computerized systems. G.S.R. 127(E) gave manufacturers with turnover up to ₹250 crore that applied in Form A until December 31, 2025. For records required by US FDA rules, 21 CFR Part 11 governs electronic records and signatures. Our automations stay outside GxP records, under change control.

    cdsco.gov.in · Source

  • BIS Quality Control Orders

    Products covered by a Quality Control Order can be made, imported or sold in India only with a BIS license or registration. Coverage changes often: many steel and electrical products are covered, while a number of chemical and polymer QCOs were rescinded in late 2025. Quote, order and private-label workflows can carry a per-product license and standard check, confirmed by the client's quality or regulatory owner against the current BIS list.

    bis.gov.in · Source

  • Messaging consent on WhatsApp, SMS and calls

    The WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy requires opt-in before a business messages someone, approved templates outside the 24-hour customer service window, and respect for every opt-out. Commercial SMS and calls in India follow TRAI's TCCCPR as amended, including in February 2025: DLT-registered headers and templates, correct categories and recorded consent and DND preferences. Order, dispatch and payment updates stay transactional; scheme promotions need prior consent.

    business.whatsapp.com · Source

  • Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020

    The four Labour Codes took effect on November 21, 2025, and the OSH Code replaced the Factories Act, 1948 among other laws. Registers, returns and inspection formats follow the central and state rules in force for each site, which differ by state during the transition, so reminders follow what the client's safety officer or occupier confirms. Automation tracks due dates; competent persons and managers sign off inspections.

    pib.gov.in · Source

Frequently asked

Do we need to replace Tally, SAP or our current ERP?

No. The ERP stays the system of record for items, prices, orders, invoices and stock. We read from it through its API, scheduled exports or a connector, and write back only drafts or status fields you approve, such as a draft sales order for the order desk. Tally Prime, SAP Business One, Dynamics 365 Business Central, NetSuite, Odoo and ERPNext setups are all common starting points.

Can you connect IndiaMART, TradeIndia and our website enquiries?

IndiaMART offers a Lead Manager API to paid sellers, which we use to pull or receive enquiries into your CRM. For other marketplaces we use whatever official API, export or email notification your subscription provides, and website forms post directly. We do not scrape marketplace dashboards or buy contact lists.

Will AI set prices, approve credit or release batches?

No. AI reads documents, extracts fields, drafts quotes and summaries, and routes work. Estimators approve prices, the sales head approves discounts, the credit controller decides holds and releases, and QA decides quality dispositions and batch release. Every approval is recorded against a named person.

We run a GMP plant. Will this affect our validated systems?

Automations sit outside validated systems. They read status through approved exports or reports, send reminders and show dashboards; they do not create, edit, approve or sign GxP records. Your QA team decides whether each workflow needs a risk assessment or validation under your change control, and for US-bound products we design with 21 CFR Part 11 in mind for any records that fall within its scope.

How do WhatsApp updates to dealers and buyers work?

We use the WhatsApp Business Platform through Meta or an approved provider. Contacts opt in, for example during dealer onboarding or when registering a machine, and business-initiated messages use templates approved by WhatsApp. Order, dispatch and payment messages stay transactional, opt-outs are honored, and each dealer number is mapped to an authorized person so ledgers and prices reach only the right people.

How long before something is live?

A first pilot usually takes four to six weeks from discovery to a working workflow with a pilot group, depending on access to the ERP and marketplace accounts and how quickly approval rules are agreed. Larger workflows such as RFQ-to-quote or batch release tracking take longer and are delivered in stages.

Where is our data kept and who can see it?

Workflows run in your cloud accounts or in environments we manage for you, in an Indian region where the tools allow. Access is role-based, margins and ledgers are hidden from roles that do not need them, credentials sit in a secrets vault, and retention periods are agreed per data type. Notices, consent records and breach response steps are designed around the DPDP Act and Rules.

How do you measure whether it worked?

We baseline the agreed KPIs during Discover, such as enquiry first-response time, quote turnaround, order entry time or batch release time, and review them with you monthly after launch. We do not promise fixed improvements in advance; the numbers come from your own data.
